result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep the five colours and then add several supporting values, so neither fully meets the rubric's call for restraint. B explains why the palette works (one accent keeps it from looking cheap), tells the user to use rust sparingly, and points to type, spacing and paper texture as the real sources of a premium feel. A is tighter and its contrast figures check out, but it gives little reason to keep the palette and spends most of its length on new colour values. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep all five colors and add only small supporting neutrals and a hover state. Neither adds new accents, gold or gradients. A explains better why the palette works: the single accent is what keeps it from looking cheap. It also points to the real sources of a premium feel (whitespace, serif type, paper texture, photos of real printed pieces) and adds a good note on keeping rust scarce. B is somewhat tighter and its contrast table is useful, but its reason for keeping the palette is thinner and its advice beyond color is a single sentence.
